title: HDB Financial Services Ltd - 544429 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HDB Financial Q2 FY27 PAT rose 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, NIM 8.23%, Stage 3 down to 2.43%, with management guiding to a near-term 8.2%+ NIM.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed disbursements up 18.7% YoY to ₹18,522 crore and PAT up 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, with Stage 3 improving YoY to 2.43%. Gross loan book grew 11.7% YoY to ₹1,24,469 crore, which management described as slow relative to disbursements because of high repayments. Sequentially, NIM was 8.23% versus 8.35% in Q1, and credit cost rose to 2.37%, with Stage 2 build-up in Asset Finance (mainly used/new CV) flagged as seasonal. The 25 bps repo hike on October 7, 2026 is the main near-term margin variable; management expects a minor impact in Q3 and aims to hold NIM at 8.2%+ in the near term.

segments.name: Enterprise Lending
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 25.5% YoY; LAP+EBL (mortgage) disbursements up 30% YoY, LAP growing about 3-3.5% QoQ. Gold loan disbursements up over 60% YoY, unsecured business loans turned slightly positive QoQ (+0.2%) after six quarters.

segments.name: Asset Finance
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicle book up 8% YoY and construction equipment up 12% YoY. New CV is hitting budget, while used CV growth is weak and is being addressed through internal actions; CV and CE drove the Stage 2 build-up.

segments.name: Consumer Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements up over 25% YoY and book up 22% YoY. Consumer durables book up 49% YoY, auto loans up 22%, relationship personal loans up 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects NIM to hold in a narrow range, targeting at least 8.2%+ in the near term and 8%+ over the long term; minor impact expected in Q3 from the 25 bps repo hike.
Disbursement trajectory expected to rise, with Q3 better than Q2 and Q4 better than Q3; management hopes Q4 shows growth in the 17-18% range, though it did not commit to a number.
Medium-term credit cost target of 2.3% +/- range; Q2 credit cost of 2.37% described as a 5 bps uptick expected to reverse.
ROA target of 2.5%+ on an annualised basis in the short to medium term.
Cost ratio expected to improve modestly while AI investments continue; management said it will not let costs balloon.
Borrowing cost of 7.04% in Q2; NCDs being raised at about 8.2-8.25%.
capex_capacity: Customer franchise at 24.8 million, up about 2 million in the last six months.
Retailer and dealer touchpoints up about 10% to 1.65 lakh+; management says it has not reduced towns served.
Headcount reduced, attributed mainly to productivity gains from automation and workflow simplification.
AI-led customer onboarding started in consumer finance; over 1 in 5 early-bucket collection calls now handled by an AI bot.
Average ticket size about ₹4.6 million for LAP and ₹1.4 million for enterprise business loans; EBL offered in more than 800 cities.
demand_pricing: LAP is primarily floating, reset monthly via a published floating reference rate (updated on the 16th of each month); ALCO reviews repricing monthly and reprices if the change is substantial.
About 55-60% of bank borrowings are linked to repo; MCLR-linked borrowings are minimal. NCD rates are about 8.2-8.25%.
Management is making calibrated repricing decisions on fixed-rate assets, with risk-adjusted returns (RAROC) guiding product pricing.
Drought declared in some Maharashtra districts; tractor exposure described as small and no crop loans held. Management is monitoring food inflation risk.
Insurance commission regulation: FY26 insurance-related fee income about ₹455 crore, roughly 0.3% of RoA; the consultation paper impact is still being assessed with FIDC and IRDAI.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset yields moderate QoQ despite strong consumer finance growth, and how will cost of funds and NIM trend if repo rises 75-100 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally about 10-12 bps higher on NIM. Management said NIM came in 1-2 bps above plan, excluding an extra day in Q2, and expects only a minor Q3 impact, with LAP floating-rate pass-through and Q3 product mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asset Finance growth weak, is the problem in new or used CV?
qa_highlights.answer: New CV is hitting budget; used CV is the issue, with a combination of internal challenges and weak market demand. Delinquencies in the older book have not yet come off.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the Stage 2 build-up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to CV, and slightly to CE, as seasonal and expected to revert in the coming quarter. Management said the rise was 9 bps QoQ and that faster book growth would have shown about 2 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will drought and macro conditions in key states affect Asset Finance and the credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is monitoring impacts, with a small tractor exposure in drought-declared areas. Credit cost is managed within 2.3% +/-, and it could fall about 5 bps next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Asset Finance growth and FY28 growth, and the risk to NIM plus fee income from the insurance commission proposal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes growth will return to the industry median, citing capacity and network readiness; FY26 disbursement growth was 3%. On fees, the company is still assessing the proposal, with ₹455 crore of insurance-related income at stake.

risks_watch: NIM sensitivity to the repo hike: about 55-60% of bank borrowings are repo-linked, and NCD rates are about 8.2%, so the cost of funds could rise if the cycle continues.
Used CV growth and the older delinquent book remain unresolved; Stage 2 build-up in CV/CE needs to reverse next quarter.
Insurance commission regulation could affect fee income (about ₹455 crore in FY26).
Drought and uneven monsoon could affect rural asset quality and food inflation.
Disbursement growth must accelerate in Q3 and Q4 for the 17-18% growth target, while high repayments are holding loan book growth back.
key_quotes: We would want to hold on to where we are as at Q2, and really come up to an 8.2 %+ at least in the near term.
On the Used piece, we ha ve had certain challenges, and that's where we have taken certain actions internally, and we expect to see a turnaround as we go through over the coming months.
So, of course, there is impact of macros. We live in the Indian heartland only, not outside.
I am very hopeful that in Q3, when we speak, we start to turn around the corner on the Asset Finance quality as well.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on H2 growth and asset quality, pointing to festive demand, LAP and gold momentum, and the Q2 credit cost uptick reversing. It was cautious on the rate cycle and used-CV recovery, repeatedly saying the NIM and cost of funds would be managed in a calibrated way and that the insurance commission proposal was still being assessed, with no numbers committed.

growth.why: Management guides disbursements to rise with Q3 above Q2 and Q4 above Q3 (Q4 hoped at 17-18% growth, uncommitted), NIM held at 8.2%+ near term, and ROA 2.5%+; backing is demand from a customer franchise up 18.4% and touchpoints up ~10%, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts are quantified, so backing is partial.
